item.title: Peaky Blinders: Uncovering the truth behind Tommy Shelby’s empire; what’s real and what’s fiction?
item.description: Peaky Blinders blends real history with fiction, drawing inspiration from Birmingham's street gangs and figures like Billy Kimber and Oswald Mosley. While the Shelby family is fictional, the show incorporates real elements of early 20th-century crime and political tensions. However, its portrayal of a vast, sophisticated criminal empire departs significantly from the more localized, fragmented reality of the original Peaky Blinders.
item.dc:creator: TOI Trending Desk

item.title: Tyler Robinson timeline mystery deepens as podcaster Baron Coleman claims Discord confession came after police custody in Charlie Kirk case
item.description: Baron Coleman’s claim about Tyler Robinson’s custody timing has raised fresh doubts in the Charlie Kirk case. The Discord confession, sent after the reported custody time, is now under question. Candace Owens has supported the claim, adding more attention. While officials stand by their version, the timeline issue is now a major talking point online.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: “Low IQs”: President slams Candace Owens, Tucker Carlson and other podcasters, calls them losers chasing cheap publicity
item.description: Donald Trump strongly criticized Tucker Carlson, Megyn Kelly, Candace Owens and Alex Jones in a Truth Social post, calling them attention-seeking and irrelevant. The four commentators had raised concerns about his approach and decisions. Trump rejected their views, saying they do not represent his supporters, making the disagreement a clear and public split within his own conservative circle.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Putin announces truce with Ukraine during Orthodox Easter celebrations
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has announced a temporary ceasefire with Ukraine for the Orthodox Easter holidays, effective from April 11th to April 12th, 2026. This move follows a similar holiday truce proposal from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. The Kremlin stated that Russian troops are instructed to cease combat operations but remain ready to counter any enemy provocations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: H-1B visa delays force blind Indian student to miss his blind sister’s wedding, story goes viral
item.description: Visually impaired Indian student Rajeev Krishna Annapragada missed his sister's wedding in India due to H-1B visa appointment delays. His inability to secure a timely appointment forced him to choose between attending the significant family event and maintaining his professional stability in the US, highlighting the human cost of immigration backlogs.

item.title: YouTuber Karl Jobst takes legal action against Billy Mitchell for defamation
item.description: YouTuber Karl Jobst has sued gaming personality Billy Mitchell for defamation, alleging false claims of fraud and illegal activity following his bankruptcy. Jobst asserts Mitchell's repeated accusations, including misuse of GoFundMe donations, have damaged his reputation and earnings. The lawsuit seeks compensation for financial losses and emotional distress, stemming from a history of conflict between the two.

item.title: 'I am not Epstein's victim': US first lady Melania Trump denies any connection with convicted sex offender
item.description: First Lady Melania Trump has issued a rare public statement, firmly denying any connection to Jeffrey Epstein and refuting claims that he introduced her to President Donald Trump. She stated she has no knowledge of Epstein's abuse and was never involved with him, nor did she visit his island or travel on his plane.

item.title: Major update in fatal MRI incident: Lawsuit filed after man gets pulled into machine with metal chain
item.description: A lawsuit has been filed over the death of Keith McAllister, who was fatally pulled into an MRI machine in New York. His widow alleges staff failed to enforce basic safety protocols, allowing him to enter with a heavy metal chain. The case raises serious questions about negligence, safety compliance, and accountability as it proceeds through the courts.
item.dc:creator: TOI Trending Desk

item.title: Katie Price gets seventh driving ban: magistrate adds 6‑month ban and fines
item.description: Katie Price has landed herself in a spot of bother once more, receiving her seventh driving ban for a six-month stretch. This latest penalty stems from her refusal to answer police inquiries regarding a speeding ticket she received on the A64. To add insult to injury, she's also been slapped with a hefty £1,044 fine for her actions.

item.title: Teen dies on Ha Giang Loop: British rider’s organs save 5 patients
item.description: A young woman from Britain, aged nineteen, lost her life after a motorcycle incident said to have happened in northern Vietnam while travelling on a break between school years. item.title: UK Heat Flips To Rain: Met Office flags 26.6°C April record; cooler, wetter days ahead
item.description: Britain experienced an unseasonable heatwave, with temperatures soaring to record highs for early April. However, this warmth is short-lived as Atlantic fronts are set to bring wet skies, strong winds, and colder air by Saturday. Meteorologists attribute these extremes to long-term climate shifts, making weather patterns more pronounced. Expect a return to typical spring conditions with rain and cooler temperatures.
